subject: Pricing benchmark & next steps — Prodigy Analytics (token economics)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@prodigy-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing benchmark & next steps — Prodigy Analytics (token economics)

Hi Daniel — great to connect this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on the call so we have alignment before I loop in legal/procurement: 

Summary of what you told us:
- Workload: real-time assistant + nightly batch rerank for search.
- Current traffic: roughly 50M tokens/month today, expected to grow to ~600M tokens/month in 12 months under your roadmap.
- Quality target: comparable to Anthropic Claude 2 / OpenAI gpt-3.5/classic open models; latency target sub-300ms median for the assistant.
- Budget band you called out: internal target $/1M tokens in the range of $6–$10 to be competitive for your lines of business.

What I’m sending with this note:
- Attached: pricing-comparison-20251112.xlsx (benchmark vs OpenAI / Anthropic / open-model hosts; draft Redwood offer).
- Short proposal below for budgeting and procurement conversations.

High-level benchmark (draft numbers for budgeting):
- OpenAI (hosted proprietary models): ~$35–$60 per 1M tokens (varies heavily by model and context length).
- Anthropic (hosted): ~$22–$38 per 1M tokens.
- Large open-model hosts (managed inference on optimized infra): ~$10–$18 per 1M tokens median.
- Self-hosted / Dedicated with aggressive quantization & reserved capacity: ~$4–$9 per 1M tokens depending on commit and model.

Redwood illustrative pricing (we can firm these up after we get final committed volumes and SLA):
- Pay-as-you-go (hosted): $10 per 1M tokens (no commit) — good for ramp/POC.
- Committed reserved capacity (12-month term, 1B tokens/mo commit): $6 per 1M tokens, includes priority capacity and 30-day retention for traces.
- Dedicated private deployment (on-prem/VPC) with sustained 1B+/mo: $5 per 1M tokens (customer-managed infra + Redwood private control plane) — requires infra sizing and onboarding.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm expected committed volume range for procurement (best guess for months 1–6, and months 7–12).
2) I’ll share a tidy price sheet + example SOW and a quick canary rollout plan for Dedicated vs Hosted.
3) If numbers look good, we can put a term sheet (non-binding) in place and engage legal — I’ll include Laura on that.

Are you available for a 30-min follow-up Friday to lock in the volume buckets and target $/1M you want in the term sheet?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0183

Thanks Sergio — useful summary and thanks for pulling the benchmarking together. A few clarifying questions before we lock a follow-up: 

1) Can you confirm the exact $/1M for each Redwood tier in the attached spreadsheet (we need a clear number for procurement).
2) Our procurement team wants to know whether Redwood can meet a target of $8 per 1M tokens if we commit to ~1B tokens/month for 12 months (this is aggressive but aligns to our internal target).
3) Any hidden fees we should budget for (eg. egress, model fine-tune hosting, additional tracing retention beyond the standard)?

Our timeline: procurement wants final pricing by 30 Nov. We have Clara (procurement) on copy — she’ll be the one signing. If you can get a straight yes/no on the $8/1M for that commit (and the assumptions), that would help us decide which internal path to take.

-Daniel

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:05:30 -0800
Subject: RE: Pricing benchmark & next steps — internal note

Internal — quick read for Sergio/Laura/Monica:

Short answer on $8/1M for 1B/mo commit: yes, we can do $8/1M but only with the following constraints to protect margin and SLA:
- 12-month committed term, invoiced monthly in arrears.
- Minimum upfront commit of 6 months of capacity sizing costs (to cover reserved GPU pool ramp).
- Model: Redwood-managed open-model variant (bert-ish assistant) or quantized Llama-derivative that we have on our optimized kernel path. Proprietary LLMs or large-context variants will be priced higher.
- Included: standard observability + 30-day traces. Additional retention or custom eval pipelines billed separately.
- Egress: first 1TB/month included; beyond that standard cloud egress rates apply (or customer supplies their own VPC peering for private).

Reasoning: with 1B tokens/month the unit compute + storage + amortized infra sits ~ $3.5–$4.5/1M before fixed overheads. At $8/1M we preserve ~30–40% gross margin once you include SRE/support and reserved capacity costs.

Recommend we present a tiered offer in the client-facing doc:
- PAYG hosted: $10 / 1M tokens (no commit)
- COMMIT 250M/mo (12mo): $8.5 / 1M
- COMMIT 1B/mo (12mo): $8.0 / 1M (with minimum onboarding/infra fee)
- DEDICATED reserved (customer infra / VPC): $5.0–$6.0 / 1M (depends on infra amortization)

I’ll draft a short pricing table and hand it to you Sergio; Laura can sign off on anything that deviates from these ranges.

—Aditya
Senior Deals
Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@prodigy-analytics.com>, Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@prodigy-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing benchmark & next steps — Prodigy Analytics (token economics)

Daniel / Clara — thanks for the fast reply. We can commit to a clear, procurement-ready pricing structure. Below is the client-facing offer and the assumptions baked in. I’ve also attached an updated two-pager and the price sheet (pricing-comparison-20251112.xlsx and redwood-offer-psa-20251112.pdf).

Redwood offer (finalized for procurement review):
- Option A — Pay-as-you-go (hosted): $10 / 1M tokens (no commit). Good for POC.
- Option B — Committed hosted (12-month term): 1B tokens/month commit -> $8 / 1M tokens. Requirements: 12-month term, standard SLO (99.5% uptime), minimum onboarding fee equal to 6 months of capacity baseline (one-time), first 1TB egress included.
- Option C — Dedicated private (VPC/on-prem): $5 / 1M tokens (assumes customer infra + standard ops support).

Benchmark context (for procurement):
- OpenAI: hosted proprietary endpoints typically range higher depending on model/context — we used ~$35–$60 / 1M as a reference for their higher-tier models.
- Anthropic: hosted; used a market range of ~$22–$38 / 1M.
- Managed open-model hosts: ~$10–$18 / 1M (these are other vendors providing hosted inference on optimized infra).

Assumptions for the $8 / 1M price:
- Commit: 1B tokens/month for 12 months.
- Model: Redwood-managed open-model variant on standard config (we'll clarify exact model family in SOW).
- SLA: 99.5% uptime, standard latency SLOs; additional premium SLAs available at uplift.
- Billing: monthly in arrears; cancellation early requires pro-rated termination fee (to be detailed in PSA).

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I’ll share a short non-binding term sheet by EOD Thursday.
2) Procurement (Clara) — can you confirm if DocuSign is the preferred route and whether you need vendor paperwork (W-9, SOC 2 attestation)?
3) Schedule a 30-min workshop to lock down expected monthly buckets (we propose a simple three-bucket plan: 0–250M / 250–1B / 1B+).

Happy to adjust language to match your procurement template. Thanks again — we’re excited to move forward.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0183
